title: The shared holdout is structurally blind to what this lane measures
finding: holdout.make_folds masks visible catalogue pixels pixel-exactly, so a prediction that moves a dot 1-3 px off a catalogue line has nothing to be credited against: the withheld target is the catalogue's own hidden segments, and a lateral shift of a traced line is not a new segment. Measured, not argued: arm B (evidence snap) 0.00012 vs arm D (random sub-pixel jitter) 0.00011, overlapping intervals.
action: Reported as a limitation of the instrument rather than a failure of the hypothesis. The lane is judged by its own pre-registered rule (corridor-level consistency) plus two nulls and a sign-flip permutation control, and the holdout is used only to rule out a catastrophe.
verified_by: evidence/holdout_corrections_v1.json

title: LiDAR layers are packed, and the packing differs between files
finding: The 100 m scarp stack (h52_scarp3m_100m.tif) is int16 with nodata -32768 and a per-band SCALE divisor; the 3 m pilot tiles are plain int16 with z_m = 1000 + value/10. Taking either at face value yields elevations near -3276 m or a 1000 m bias.
action: Decoding asserted against each file's own metadata and bounds at load time, plus a valid-fraction guard that raises when a reprojection returns less than 90% valid data (the failure mode that silently produced all-NaN tiles during development).
verified_by: rasterio metadata + values read in this workspace

title: The duplicate-submission rule as written is vacuous against dense rasters
finding: The lane protocol says: if >70% of my dots lie within 3 px of one registry raster's dots, log a duplicate and stop. Sibling repos publish whole-footprint plausibility masks (5,167,373 and 4,830,583 dotted cells). Against those, ANY non-empty submission is 100% contained, so the rule fires on every candidate in the corpus, including files that are not submissions at all. The reverse overlap for the same pairs was 0.01-0.12%. The authoritative run confirms it: gates.lane_uniqueness_report on the final primary dots returns max Spearman 0.0051 (pass, threshold 0.90) but directed <=3px proximity 1.000 against a 0.70 threshold, duplicate=true, ok=false, 105 offending priors -- because the raster carries a single dot. The sensitivity raster (14 dots) triggers 31 priors on the same criterion and 0 in the reciprocal direction.
action: Both directions plus the reciprocal minimum are computed for all 485 rasters (evidence/registry_screen_v1_rows.jsonl), the trigger is reported with the prior's dot count so a reader can see which priors are density masks, and the site does not claim a clean uniqueness pass. The rule's *intent* -- do not resubmit someone's raster -- is additionally served by the emission rule never placing a dot on a catalogue pixel. The gate's own verdict is published on the site banner and in the run card as a failure, and no slot is claimed for either raster. [2026-10-09 update: re-run on the full 944-raster corpus (scripts/screen_registry.py, evidence/registry_screen_v1.json): the forward rule triggers for 292 of 944 (candidate, prior) pairs across both rasters, 141 of them dense layers; reciprocal overlap above 0.70 is 0 and the reverse fraction peaks at 0.0011. The rule as written is still the stop condition, so the lane stops as a duplicate; the rule itself is flagged for a protocol-level fix.]
verified_by: scripts/screen_registry.py over /home/user/_reg

title: The first offset result was an instrument artifact, not a finding
finding: Before calibration, the median absolute catalogue-to-crest offset was 0.656 px and looked like a small real displacement. Two null controls showed a random point with no fault anywhere is 'nearest crest' 0.49 px away and catalogue pixels sampled in a random direction 0.52 px away: the signal was inside the noise floor of the estimator.
action: Null-calibrated gates became mandatory for every statistic in this lane (crest height floor = 90th percentile of the null), the histogram is published next to both nulls, and the sign-flip permutation control was added for the cluster rule.
verified_by: evidence/calibration_v1.json, evidence/cluster_gate_control.json

title: Corridor z-scores explode when the MAD collapses
finding: The robust SE of a median goes to zero when four corroborated pixels share a value, so z = |median|/SE reached 60.6 on one component -- arithmetically true, scientifically meaningless.
action: corridor_table now takes sigma_floor_px and floors the SE at the measured disagreement between a 100 m offset and the same offset measured on 3 m LiDAR (1.296 px). With the floor the same corridor's z is bounded by the instrument's precision. No z is quoted anywhere in this repo without that floor.
verified_by: evidence/lidar_calibration_v1.json estimator block

title: A sign-asymmetric crest detector in the lane's own code (found by a test, fixed here)
finding: Three defects were caught while writing contract tests against synthetic scarps of known position: (a) the PCA strike vector had an arbitrary sign, so neighbouring pixels of one trace could place corrected dots on opposite sides; (b) the second difference was taken at 0.25 px sample spacing on bilinearly interpolated data, which turns the interpolation's piecewise linearity into a comb of curvature spikes one cell apart, and the 'nearest crest' rule then selected a spike instead of the scarp; (c) the prominence test measured a crest against its own flanking concave lobe, which exists only on one side of the trace, so right-hand scarps were rejected and left-hand ones accepted. (b) and (c) both shrink the offset histogram toward zero -- i.e. they could manufacture exactly the negative verdict this lane reported.
action: Fixed in src/gems56/corrections.py (lane code, not a vendored template module, so no shared-tool fork was created): strike canonicalisation, a one-cell curvature baseline with a widened sampling window, full-kernel-support requirement, and a relative-strength rule symmetric in the sign of the offset. All of E1, E1c, E2, E3 and the uniqueness screen were then re-run from scratch. The remaining known bias (+0.2 to +0.5 px, constant in offset, shape-dependent) is characterised in evidence/estimator_validation.json and is why no claim here rests on an absolute sub-pixel offset.
verified_by: tests/test_contracts.py (10 tests) + scripts/validate_estimator.py

title: Our rasters write 0.0 outside the data extent; the official sample writes NaN
finding: The format page says cells outside the provided data extent should be null or NaN, and sample_submission.tif does exactly that (7,111,787 NaN cells of 12,279,160). The rasters built here carry 0.0 in that region instead, because the shared template tool enforces an all-finite export policy: gates.format_report appends 'NaN/infinite pixels: fail our all-finite export policy (public spec permits outside-footprint NaN)' and submission_writer.write_submission refuses a prediction that is not finite. So this is a deliberate template decision that contradicts the organizer's sentence, not an oversight of this lane's.
action: Measured the consequence rather than assuming it: under DTI, FPw sums only over prediction pixels with p > 0, so 0 and null outside are arithmetically identical, and both are inside [0,1], which is what the upload range check enforces. Kept the template behaviour so this lane's file is byte-comparable with the sibling submissions that already uploaded, published the exact difference on the site instead of claiming compliance, and recorded the flip: writing out[~valid]=nan with nodata=nan in submission_writer (one edit, shared tool) if DrivenData ever rejects a 0-filled exterior. A reviewer with an account should confirm which convention the platform's validator prefers.
verified_by: independent rasterio read of both rasters and of the sample: non-null-outside-footprint count 12,218,172, sample NaN count 7,111,787

title: Under the official metric, a 14-dot file cannot beat 0.2778 unless the hidden positive set is under ~558 pixels
finding: DTI ≤ T_max/(0.2·T_max + 0.8·|G|) with T_max = min(|G|, S·K), K = 9.3803 (sum of the triangular kernel over the 29-cell disc). For S = 14 this gives 0.0129 at |G| = 12,691 and 0.0027 at |G| = 60,988. The hidden |G| is not published.
action: Recorded as the main negative result of the lane. Recommendation: do not spend a weekly slot on this lane's file. Leader route requires dense recall-weighted emission, which is outside this lane's method paragraph.
verified_by: gems56.metric.OFFSETS, formula from the official page (DERIVED)

title: Band 6 'tc' description is ambiguous and the data are magnitude-like
finding: evidence/grid.json's own band inventory says band 6 is 'tc - Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection'. Measured this session: values span 2.95-88.57 with NO sign change (p1 7.72, p50 18.48, p99 29.10), so the classic tilt-angle zero-crossing rule cannot be applied literally -- either the band is total curvature (>=0) or it is a magnitude of tilt. A hypothesis written as 'zero contour of tc' would be wrong on the bytes.
action: H8 in docs/research/hypotheses-20261009.md is written as proximity to LOW tc rather than a signed zero crossing, and the ambiguity is carried in the hypothesis text.
verified_by: read of data/training_features.tif band 6 (this session, scripts of E1); evidence/grid.json band_descriptions

title: Footprint-edge fake features in the shared transforms (scarp_step / hessian_line / gradient_magnitude / rank01)
finding: The transforms zero-fill outside the footprint before differencing or smoothing. Measured on the real footprint: scarp_step on iso_grav_anom returns median 5.28 on the 23,600-cell rim band vs 0.47 in the interior (p99 29.6 vs 2.1), and 56.5% of the top-25,000 cells of the ranked field landed on that rim band -- i.e. the data edge itself was the strongest 'fault'. A second-order effect: rank01 pushed NaN-within-valid cells into the top histogram bin (rank ~1.0), so edge-masking a transform without fixing rank01 would have re-created the same artefact. This defect invalidated the first E1 run (evidence/holdout_discovery_v0_prefx.json): every physics arm scored below the chance control while emitting mostly on the rim.
action: Fixed ONCE in the shared template src/gems56/transform.py (allowed by the protocol, no private fork): scarp_step now requires full two-sided + persistence support inside the footprint; hessian_line masks a 3-sigma edge band; gradient_magnitude masks cells at distance <2 px from the complement; rank01 excludes NaN-inside-valid from the ranking and keeps them NaN. Six regression tests added in tests/test_transform_edges.py (each fails pre-fix). E1 re-run with identical pre-registered design; the pre-fix receipt is preserved as evidence/holdout_discovery_v0_prefx.json.
verified_by: tests/test_transform_edges.py (6 tests); the rim-vs-interior measurement printed in this session's log; re-run receipt evidence/holdout_discovery_v1.json

what: On the round-2 dots-phase gate (evidence/lane_gate_discovery_v2.json) the literal brief rule '>70% of my dots within 3 px of ONE registry raster's dots' fires against 22 informative (non-probe) priors, and the coverage-adjusted policy agrees (DUPLICATE/STOP both). The trigger is density-degenerate: for every one of the 22, near_frac is within +/-0.03 of that prior's own 3 px halo coverage of the eligible grid (e.g. 0.887 vs 0.861, 0.740 vs 0.759, 0.700 vs 0.735), i.e. the clause is satisfied by any dot set whatever, exactly as IR-56-006 showed the same clause is vacuous at 1-dot counts against near-universal priors. The agreement tests pass: max Spearman 0.043 on the dots and 0.193 on the surface vs the 0.90 bar, zero identical hashes, and the screen's reciprocal >0.70 count is 0.
why_it_matters: Read literally, a raster whose 3 px halo covers >=70% of the grid makes the '>70% of my dots near it' clause unfailable for ANY candidate, so a STOP verdict carries no information about lane drift at that density; the mirror-image defect (IR-56-006) makes the same clause unfailable in the other direction at tiny dot counts.
action: Protocol executed as written: the verdict DUPLICATE/STOP is logged, nothing is promoted, and the candidate was already NEGATIVE on the holdout. The defect is reported rather than argued around; both directions are shown side by side in the receipt (surface PASS, dots STOP). No gate code was modified to change the outcome.
